note: He is the purest good-to-great case in the corpus — the rep offered the ICP's own phrase and the prospect took it ("Sounds like you want to go from good to great" — "Yeah, pretty much. That's a good way to put it") — self-scored 7.5-8 out of 10, and articulate about wanting the last 20%. He is nowhere near the deconditioned exclusion: ten years of consistent training, a half marathon in February, 190 lb at 5'10" down from 250. But he fails the income test in the most concrete way available: sticker shock at the number ("I didn't think it was going to be that high"), a request for a month or two to get the money together, and a consumer finance application declined live on the call despite an 822 Equifax score. And health is not his neglected area — it is the area he has been most disciplined about for a decade, while the deficit he brought is knowledge and programming. Occupation was never established at any point, so 'successful' cannot be assessed and sits in neither list, which is itself a finding: the rep priced a $6,000 offer without ever learning what the man does for a living. The pattern this call adds to the corpus is that the stated ICP's income criterion is doing real work — it correctly predicted the stall — while good_to_great, the criterion the rep leans on out loud, predicted nothing.
